newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Spratlys row shadows visit by China's Chi to Manila.
newsitem.headline: Spratlys row shadows visit by China's Chi to Manila.

text.p: Chinese Defence Minister Chi Haotian arrived in Manila on Friday for a six-day visit to the Philippines shadowed by the two countries' rival claims to the Spratly Islands.
Chi will meet President Fidel Ramos and other Philippine officials, visit a World War Two allied fortress and a former U.S. naval base which Manila has turned into a bustling freeport.
China said in an statement that strengthening of relations between the two countries and their armed forces "conduces peace and stability of the Asia-Pacific region."
"We would like to make our positive efforts to promote the constant development of friendly and cooperative relations between our two countries and two militaries," he added.
A lingering dispute over the Spratly Islands has shadowed relations between the two countries.
A cluster of potentially oil-rich isles, reefs and shoals in the South China Sea, the area is wholly or partly claimed by China, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia and Brunei.
Tensions flared in 1995 when the Philippines accused China of building what it said looked like naval support structures on the Manila-claimed Mischief Reef.
The Chinese, who claim all of the Spratlys, said the structures were shelters for fishermen.

The Chinese embassy in December criticised the Philippine military's reopening of an airstrip on one of the islands which Manila claims and urged the Philippines not to take any action that would harm bilateral relations.

Despite the row both sides have taken pains not to escalate tensions. In talks in Manila last November, Chinese President Jiang Zemin and President Fidel Ramos agreed to set aside the dispute and work instead for ways at developing the area.

On Saturday Chi will visit the former U.S. naval facility at Subic Bay, now a thriving freeport, and on Tuesday tour historic Corregidor island on Manila Bay which U.S. and allied forces used as a fortress against Japanese forces during World War Two.
Chi is to meet Ramos on Wednesday before he leaves for Indonesia on Thursday.
